summary: Cut fresh database initialisation cost (#136) (#151)
details: * perf(db): cut fresh database initialisation cost (#136) A fresh test database spent ~1.25 s in `initializeDatabase`, called 18 times per suite (~22 s). Index creation dominated: 92 `createIndex` calls, each a journal commit on a newly created collection. - Group the index catalogue by collection and send one `createIndexes` command per collection (46 commands). Keys, names, uniqueness, partial filters, TTL and `expireAfterSeconds` are unchanged; a failed grouped command falls back to per-index creation so one legacy conflict cannot block the rest, as before. - Bulk-write the 78 baseline policies instead of one upsert per record. - Split startup into `ensureDatabaseIndexes` (new `src/lib/db-indexes.ts`) and `seedBaselineContent`. `initializeDatabase` still runs both, so production startup and `getDatabase` are unchanged. Mongo tests that seed their own content use the schema half; notification-outbox keeps the full path and asserts the seeded register and indexes. - The in-memory preview implements `createIndexes` and `bulkWrite`. Verified on the local replica set: index phase 1.44 s -> 0.76 s and total 1.27 s -> 0.95 s over six interleaved pairs (shared host, so absolute wall time varied). A fresh database has the same 47 collections and 139 indexes, and the same 78 proposals and revisions, before and after. Full suite (833 tests) passed twice; each run left only `admin`, `config`, `engage` and `local`. * chore(changelog): record database initialisation change (#136) * fix(settings): tie-break site settings events by insertion order * chore(changelog): record the site event ordering fix

summary: Bound comment vote retries by time, not attempt count (#123) (#134)
details: * fix(discussion): bound comment vote retries by time with backoff (#123) The comment vote compare-and-swap gave up after 12 fixed attempts with a 2-8 ms jitter. On a cold replica set the first write can take hundreds of milliseconds, so 25 concurrent voters exhausted the attempts and valid votes failed with 'Comment votes changed at the same time. Try again.' Retry on a five-second time budget instead, with exponential backoff and jitter (4 ms doubling to a 250 ms cap). Legitimate contention converges even when writes are slow; a genuinely stuck writer still fails in bounded time. Exactly-once is unchanged. The write is still one version-filtered compare-and-swap of the whole vote state, so a lost race writes nothing and retries against the committed state. Voter arrays, switching between upvotes and downvotes, and the persisted shape are untouched. Expiry now logs comment_vote_retry_budget_exhausted with the comment ID, attempt count and budget only - never member IDs or vote choices - before throwing. Tests add a deterministic cold-write case (40 ms per comment write) that fails under the old attempt count and passes now, plus a stuck-writer case proving the budget is bounded and the warning is emitted without identities. * chore(changelog): record bounded comment vote retries (#123) Regenerates the public snapshot so the fix commit appears on /changelog/. The 80-commit window still drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96. * fix(discussion): make the comment vote retry budget configurable (#123) The 5 s retry budget was a fixed constant. Under full-suite load the injected 40 ms cold-write test needed longer than 5 s to converge and failed, even though votes were not actually lost. Read the budget from ENGAGE_COMMENT_VOTE_RETRY_BUDGET_MS at call time. Unset, empty or invalid values use the 5000 ms default; values are clamped to 250-60000 ms so a bad setting cannot remove the bound. The expiry warning records the effective budget. The stress test now runs with a 15000 ms budget, proving convergence under injected slow writes on a loaded machine while production keeps the 5 s default. The stuck-writer test uses the 250 ms floor so it stays fast, and asserts the default, fallback and clamp rules. Exactly-once is unchanged: the write is still one version-filtered compare-and-swap of the whole vote state, and no persisted shape or privacy boundary changed. * chore(changelog): record the configurable comment vote retry budget (#123) Regenerates the public snapshot so the stabilisation commit appears on /changelog/. * refactor(discussion): inject the comment vote retry budget instead of an environment variable (#123) Configuration belongs in the administration panel; environment variables are reserved for secrets, bootstrap and deployment topology. Remove ENGAGE_COMMENT_VOTE_RETRY_BUDGET_MS from the vote path. The production budget stays a fixed 5000 ms module constant. Tests pass an explicit optional fifth argument to voteOnComment, an injection point that is validated and clamped to 250-60000 ms; production callers omit it. The expiry warning still records the effective budget. The concurrency tests pass 15000 ms so a loaded runner cannot turn a machine stall into a false failure, and the stuck-writer test passes 1 ms (clamped to the 250 ms floor) so it stays fast. Exactly-once assertions, the persisted shape and the privacy boundary are unchanged. Docs remove the environment-override wording. * chore(changelog): record the injected comment vote retry budget (#123) Regenerates the public snapshot so the refactor appears on /changelog/. * chore(changelog): record bounded comment vote retries after merging main

summary: Remove the tally projection watermark and make rebuilds compare-and-set only (#124)
details: * fix(ballots): make the tally projection rebuild compare-and-set only The merged projection skipped increments whose vote timestamp was at or below an appliedThrough watermark that a rebuild believed it had counted. Under concurrency that watermark was wrong: a vote could be visible to the increment but not the recount, so the increment was skipped and the row under-counted. The full suite failed on main with 7 votes in the row against 8 votes. Remove appliedThrough and its timestamp guard entirely. Increments always apply: each is one atomic upsert of the choice, total and an internal monotonic version. Nothing is skipped. The rebuild is now absolute and compare-and-set only. It reads the row version (0 when the row is missing), recounts every bound vote, and writes absolute counts only if the version is unchanged, advancing it by one. A mismatch recounts and retries, bounded. A concurrent increment either lands before the recount (the absolute write is correct) or after the compare-and-set (it adds on top). The 500 ms deadline still writes nothing, leaving the row for the repair CLI. Revision moves remain transactional deltas and certification still never reads the projection. Tests: 20 rounds that deterministically interleave an increment between the rebuild's recount and its compare-and-set (and after it), asserting exact equality with the authoritative bound tally every round; an increment after an absolute rebuild is applied; the concurrent first-vote, change and revision-move cases remain. summary: Paginate the public list and add a display-only tally projection (#52) (#112)
details: * feat(ballots): project display-only tallies after a committed vote Public list pages (/ and /proposals/) tallied every vote and decrypted every encrypted ballot just to show a count. Add a display-only ballot_tallies row per (ballotId, revisionId), written best-effort after the vote transaction commits. The projection is never authoritative: recordFormalDecision keeps recomputing the outcome from the bound votes and does not read it. A failed or slow projection write is logged as an operational event and cannot fail, delay or alter the vote. Vote changes decrement the previous choice and increment the new one, a re-cast of the same choice is a no-op, and rows are revision-scoped. The row stores counts and a timestamp only: no member id, choice, reason or envelope. listProposals can now omit vote tallies so public reads never touch proposal_votes; the web pages overlay certified results and the projection in the next commit. Adds the unique compound index to initializeDatabase and a rebuild/repair path for the CLI. Refs #52 * perf(proposals): paginate the public list and stop scanning ballots /proposals/ loaded every proposal, applied search, stage, branch and sort in the page, and decrypted every vote for the row totals. It now reads a bounded display page of 25 rows from MongoDB with server-side pagination. - Page, total, page count and range are computed from the filtered set; invalid or out-of-range pages clamp; ties order deterministically by proposal id. - Links keep q, stage, branch, space, sort, focus and joined; changing a filter starts at page 1. Pagination uses the Button primitive with previous/next and a live range status. - Each page self-references its canonical address and emits rel=prev/rel=next. The repository has no noIndex convention for parameterised lists, so pages stay indexable with a self-canonical rather than inventing one. - Rows no longer read proposal_votes. A certified ballot shows the tally stored on ballot_results; otherwise a fresh ballot_tallies row is used; a missing or stale row shows "Voting open — tally updating" with a link to the matter. - / overlays the same projection on the register it already reads, so home no longer decrypts votes either. Matters without a trustworthy aggregate are left out of the highlights rather than showing a wrong percentage. Visibility is still decided by canViewProposal and re-checked after the coarse MongoDB pre-filter; eligibility, ballot binding and deadlines are untouched. Refs #52 * feat(scripts): rebuild the ballot tally projection from votes Add npm run ballots:tally-projection. It reports missing, mismatched and orphan projection rows against the votes they should represent, and with --apply rebuilds them. It never deletes, edits or rewrites a vote and never certifies a result. Dry run is the default; --verify exits non-zero when rows need repair; an explicit --database is required; production writes additionally require --allow-production and --confirm-production engage_production. Encrypted votes need the ballot keys and the tool refuses to write a partial tally without them. Refs #52 * fix(proposals): keep the active stage tab and certified tallies correct The parsed stage is now '' rather than 'all' for an unfiltered list, so the All tab has to compare against '' to stay marked current. A certified result is authoritative even when the matter no longer carries a ballotRevisionId (for example after a zero-vote unbind). Resolve certified results by every visible matter's ballot, not only those with a current binding, so the row shows the recorded tally instead of falling back to no tally. Refs #52 * docs(status): record public list pagination and the tally projection Adds the before/after harness snapshots for / and /proposals/ (before 57402f0, after 65ace21) and records what changed: 25-row server pagination with filter preservation and canonical/rel links, a display-only ballot_tallies projection, certified tallies from ballot_results, and a neutral tally-updating state for missing or stale rows. The profiler window records 3 -> 0 proposal_votes operations on /proposals/ and 6 -> 0 on /, with getMore batches falling from three to one on every measured public page. Reports the /proposals/ HTML increase honestly: it renders 25 rows instead of 15 at the specified page size, not extra markup per row. Updates I12 and S4, notes the detail page's remaining live tally and the deployment step to backfill the projection, and adds the new collection and CLI to the architecture docs. Refs #52 * fix(ballots): move a re-bound amendment tally to the right revision row An amendment ballot can be re-bound to a newer wording revision. A member who had already voted on the previous revision casts again on the new one, so the previous count belongs to the old row, not the new row. The projection now learns the revision the previous vote was bound to and recounts both rows from their votes instead of applying a delta to the wrong row. Main matter ballots cannot reach this path: castVote refuses a ballot whose existing votes are not all bound to its current revision. Adds a projection test for the move. Refs #52 * docs(status): correct the public-list suite count The final run includes the revision-move projection test: 655 tests, 0 fail. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record public list pagination and the tally projection Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. Refs #52 * fix(ballots): make tally projection writes atomic under concurrency The projection's first-vote path read the votes and wrote absolute counts when no row existed. A concurrent increment could land between that read and write, or after it, double counting; the full suite exposed it as an extra abstain. The normal path is now one atomic upsert increment, so a first vote creates the row and counts it in a single operation. Two concurrent first votes can no longer each create a row or lose one. A write conflict from a transactional revision move retries inside the deadline. The only remaining recount is for an unreadable prior vote and the repair CLI. It is compare-and-set guarded on an internal version token and bounded by a watermark recorded in appliedThrough, so an increment for a vote the recount already included is skipped, and an increment that landed first forces a fresh recount. The deadline is enforced before each write (and with maxTimeMS on the recount), so a timed-out rebuild leaves the row for the repair CLI instead of writing a stale absolute count. A revision move is two transactional deltas on the old and new rows, not a recount. A row whose counts are negative or do not sum to its total is never displayed; it reads as tally pending until repaired. Tests: many concurrent first votes, concurrent vote changes and a concurrent revision move each equal the authoritative tally; ten rebuild-versus-increment races; a recorder that a timed-out rebuild writes nothing; and the public list treating an inconsistent row as pending. Refs #52 * docs(status): record the race-safe projection write strategy Replaces the read-then-write description with the atomic strategy: an upsert increment for normal votes, transactional deltas for a revision move, and a compare-and-set recount bounded by a watermark and deadline for the last-resort path. Records that an internally inconsistent row is displayed as pending, the residual out-of-order watermark caveat, the concurrency tests and both full suite results. Refs #52 * chore(changelog): record the race-safe tally projection writes Regenerates the public snapshot from this branch's history. The generator's fixed 80-commit window drops the oldest entries, which is the pre-existing truncation tracked in #96, not a decision in this slice. summary: Paginate the proposal register and stop reading ballots (#52) (#103)
details: * perf(admin): paginate the proposal register and stop reading ballots The proposals register loaded every proposal, including its rationale, and decrypted every vote for the rows in Decide so it could show live tallies. It sent ~1 MB of HTML and did per-vote work on a list read. The register now reads a bounded page of 25 rows from MongoDB, ordered by proposal id, with search, stage and branch filters applied server-side and the viewer's branch scope preserved. Page links keep the active filters; changing a filter starts at page 1; invalid or out-of-range pages clamp. Pagination uses the existing Button primitive with previous/next, the current page and a status region announcing the visible range. `listProposalRegister` projects the register fields only (no `details` or `detailHtml`) and never touches `proposal_votes`, so no ballot is decrypted on a list read. For a certified ballot it shows the tally, computed result and rule basis stored on `ballot_results` at certification. An open ballot shows "Open — view ballot" instead of live counts, and a closed but uncertified ballot links to the workspace to record the outcome. The detail workspace keeps the live bound tally and the result form unchanged; recording from the list would require decrypting every vote. Editing, revising and creating still resolve their full record, including rationale, from any page, with the same scope and lock checks. Measured with `npm run perf:render` (78 synthetic proposals, 1200 votes, 3 runs, administrator): HTML 938,422 B → 283,915 B (−69.7%); document DB commands 19 → 16; document DB time 28.7 ms → 16.0 ms; TTFB 103.1 ms → 57.6 ms. A MongoDB profiler window shows the register request reads proposals, comments, ballot_results, ballots, amendments and revisions, and no `proposal_votes`. Refs #52. * fix(admin): keep legacy register records keyed by policyId and status Legacy proposal documents store the identifier, stage and topic space under `policyId`, `status` and `category`. The register's narrow projection only asked for the current field names, so the shared normaliser would have seen an empty identifier and defaulted the stage to Deliberate. Project the alias fields too (still excluding rationale and ballot data), and match the stage filter against a stored `status` when a document has no `stage`. Adds a regression case for a legacy-shaped record: it keeps its identifier, its normalised stage, its space, and remains searchable by rationale without returning it. Refs #52. * docs(status): record register pagination and the tally-free list read Adds the before/after harness snapshots for `/admin/proposals/` (base `78c07c0`, after `c1f72c0`) and records what the register now reads and shows: one 25-row projected page, no `proposal_votes` access, certified tallies from `ballot_results`, and links instead of live counts for uncertified ballots. Records the trade-offs honestly: inline outcome recording moved to the workspace, "Open amendments" counts the whole register rather than the filtered subset, and search moved into MongoDB while still matching rationale. Updates I12/#52 without claiming the member-facing vote scans are done, and notes the small in-memory database fidelity improvements from this slice. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for register pagination Regenerates the public changelog from this branch's history: the register pagination, the legacy-record fix and the audit/status updates appear as the newest entries. summary: Response headers, hash-based CSP and cross-origin enforcement (#38) (#100)
details: * feat(security): add perimeter headers, CSP and cross-site request rule Every response now carries nosniff, a strict referrer policy, frame denial, a minimal Permissions-Policy and a Content Security Policy. HSTS is sent only in production when HTTPS is provable. The policy keeps Astro's build-time script and style hashes and allows only the external hosts the app uses: Cloudflare Turnstile (script, frame, connect) and the first-party Plausible host (script, connect). Inline style attributes are allowed through style-src-attr only, because tally and progress bars use them; script-src has no unsafe-inline and no directive permits unsafe-eval. The service-worker registration was is:inline, which Astro does not hash, so it is now a processed script. Astro's form-post origin check is kept, and allowedDomains trusts the production host over HTTPS so its comparison uses the public origin behind the proxy. The middleware adds what Astro's check deliberately exempts: every state-changing method, JSON bodies, a cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site, an Origin that differs from the trusted public origin, and an absent Origin when a session or dev cookie is present. Bearer cron calls and webhooks carry no cookie and stay allowed. Chromium checks the home, proposal, sign-in and Sense Box pages for CSP violations, console errors and failed requests; proves the Turnstile script and frame and the Plausible script and event endpoint reach the network layer; asserts the document and JSON header sets; and shows same-origin fetches and native form posts succeed while browser, JSON and cookie-without-Origin state-changing requests are refused. Cloudflare and Plausible are intercepted and answered locally; the script never contacts production.
